data.narrative:
Lilac Solutions is a Series C-stage climate and energy company that has raised $315M to date. The valuation analysis draws on two applicable methods triangulated against a peer set of three same-sector, same-stage private companies (KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy) alongside one public comparable (Lienzo, ticker LNZA) and a broader universe of eight private frontier-tech peers in energy and climate.

The Stage-Progression method applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier to the $315M total raised proxy, implying a valuation of $536M. The Peer-Median method anchors to the median valuation of the three Climate & Energy Series C comparables at $1.0B, with a range spanning $700M (Amogy) to $3.0B (KoBold Metals). This dispersion reflects meaningful variation in technology risk and commercial progress within the peer set.

Triangulating these two methods yields a median implied valuation of $768M, with a low bound of $455M (weighted toward the stage-progression approach) and a high bound of $1.1B (weighted toward peer medians). The $455M–$1.1B range reflects the tension between capital-raised-based anchoring and market-based peer comparables. Key uncertainties include the appropriate weighting between stage progression and peer benchmarking, given the wide spread in peer valuations, and whether Lilac's specific technology and pathway to commercialization justify positioning above or below the $1.0B peer median.
